messages:
alicia: Heads-up — Customer ACME just flagged a big p99 spike hitting our /generate with tool-calls enabled. Started ~11:05 PDT, p99 ~1.6s (baseline ~120ms). Repro steps + logs below.

kevin: Thanks. Do we know if this is the tool-router or the JSON schema validator taking the hit?

sylvia: Customer says it correlates with function calls that have large responses (200-1500 tokens) that get validated against the output schema.

maya: From a quick glance at sampling in traces, request enters tool-router -> schema-validate -> postprocess. The schema-validate span is long (~1.2s) on many traces.

kevin: Can you paste an example trace / span IDs?

alicia: Here's a successful trace and a slow one (redacted):

Slow trace spans:
- tool-router.process (start 0ms, end 1600ms)
  - model.generate (0ms, 180ms)
  - schema-validator.validate (200ms, 1400ms)  <-- big chunk
  - formatter.apply (1400ms, 1600ms)

Fast trace spans:
- tool-router.process (0ms, 140ms)
  - model.generate (0ms, 120ms)
  - schema-validator.validate (120ms, 130ms)
  - formatter.apply (130ms, 140ms)

kevin: That strongly suggests schema-validator is the hot path. Any recent changes to validator code or schema sizes?

sam: We rolled out schema tightening for structured output last week (2026-03-05) — introduced deeper recursive checks and full JSONPath evaluation. Could be the culprit.

oncall-sre: Paging @maya @kevin — customer SLA impacted. We should triage and apply a mitigation ASAP.

maya: Agreed. Mitigation options: 1) Toggle off strict schema validation for the affected customer route (fastest). 2) Short-circuit validator for responses > X tokens and fall back to lightweight shape-check. 3) Rollback schema change and redeploy.

kevin: For immediate relief, option 1 is lowest-risk. We can flip a per-route feature flag in Console -> route settings. I'll prepare a PR for option 2 as a medium-term fix.

alicia: Customer wants a repro they can run so they can test after we change. Example curl they used:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-2-large","prompt":"fetch invoice list","tools":[{"name":"get_invoices"}],"output_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"invoices":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"id":{"type":"string"},"amount":{"type":"number"}}}}}}'

kevin: Thanks. I'll toggle strict validation off for /routes/acme-prod-1 and monitor p95/p99. Will post timestamps of the toggle.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-09T18:12:03Z — feature-flag/admin-toggle applied to route acme-prod-1 by kevin.

maya: After toggle, preliminary metrics from synthetic traffic show p99 dropped to ~160ms for same set — promising.

alicia: Customer confirmed reduced latency in their test after ~15 minutes. They reported error-free responses so far. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Next steps: (1) ship a targeted validator optimization PR (use streaming validation + early exit on key mismatch) — I'll own. (2) Add opt-in heuristic: if response tokens > 800, use fast-shape-checker. (3) Longer-term: switch validator to incremental JSONPath engine.

sam: I'll open an internal tracking ticket and assign a priority. Ticket: INF-5123 — "Schema validator p99 regression / optimize and fallback".

oncall-sre: Also propose adding telemetry: per-validate latency histogram and schema-size tag so we can alert when validation > 200ms more often than baseline.

kevin: Agreed. I'll add the histogram metric (validate.latency_ms) and a tag validate.schema_size_chars.

alicia: Filing a customer incident note and CC'ing ACME. Thanks team.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0039 — Customer ACME latency spike. Assigned to kevin, maya.

sylvia: Closing loop with customer: want to schedule a follow-up in 24h to confirm no regressions and to share mitigation plan.

kevin: Will follow up with a short postmortem and timeline: 1) immediate toggle (done), 2) medium-term PR (ETA 4d), 3) permanent fix + perf tests (ETA 2w).

alicia: Thanks all. I'll update the customer and mark as 'mitigated' in the CRM once the medium-term PR lands.

maya: FYI for oncall: if we see another spike before PR, enable route-level batching limit to reduce concurrent validation pressure.

kevin: copying suggested metrics and the repro curl to INF-5123.

alicia: :tada: Good job, team.
